items.title: Harry Shields Interview, 1961-05-28
items.q: And my brother Jimmy, who was a very good musician, the one I told you that played all the strings and the cornet, well, he had never tried to play a clarinet, but he did finger it and he figured it out. So he helped me along with the clarinet.

ctx.x: Buffet. About how many keys do you remember? Thirteen keys. Thirteen, yeah. I've seen some of those.

Then, uh, after he, uh, went up north, he was in Chicago. Of course, I knew quite a bit about the clarinet then, but I didn't own one. How old were you when you started, about? About that time, when he first started me off, I was just a little fellow about eight years old, And he'd teach me a few little simple tunes on the clarinet. But then when he left home, I didn't have a clarinet and didn't play at all. So, uh, when he got to Chicago, man, of course I was a few years older then, I decided I wanted to…
Did you learn to read at that time ever?
